sa30:1.2: The Buddha was staying at the Squirrels’ Bamboo Grove of Rājagṛha.
sa30:1.3: Venerable Śāriputra was on Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa at the time.
sa30:2.1: There was then a prominent man’s son named Śroṇa who went for walks every day.
sa30:2.2: He went to Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa and visited Venerable Śāriputra there.
sa30:2.3: After asking how he were doing, Śroṇa withdrew to sit to one side and said to Śāriputra,
sa30:2.4: “Suppose ascetics and brahmins say this about forms that are impermanent, changing, and insecure:
sa30:2.5: ‘I am better,’ ‘I am equal,’ or ‘I am inferior.’
sa30:2.6: Why would an ascetic or brahmin form such an idea and not see them truly?
sa30:2.7: Suppose an ascetic or brahmin says about feelings … conceptions … volitions … instances of awareness that are impermanent, changing, and insecure:
sa30:2.8: ‘I am better,’ ‘I am equal,’ or ‘I am inferior.’
sa30:2.9: Why would an ascetic or brahmin form such an idea and not see them truly?
sa30:3.1: “Suppose an ascetic or brahmin says about forms that are impermanent, changing, and insecure:
sa30:3.2: ‘I am better,’ ‘I am equal,’ or ‘I am inferior.’
sa30:3.3: How do they imagine that and not see them truly?
sa30:3.4: Suppose they say about feelings … conceptions … volitions … instances of awareness that are impermanent, changing, and insecure:
sa30:3.5: ‘I am better,’ ‘I am equal,’ or ‘I am inferior.’
sa30:3.6: How do they imagine that and not see them truly?”
sa30:6.1: “Śroṇa, if something is impermanent, is that painful?”
sa30:8.1: “Śroṇa, if something is impermanent and painful, it’s subject to change.
sa30:8.3: Would a noble disciple see form as self, different from self, or that either is present in the other?”
sa30:10.2: Is feeling … conception … volition … awareness permanent or impermanent?”
sa30:12.1: “If something is impermanent, is that painful?”
sa30:14.1: “Śroṇa, if awareness is impermanent and painful, then it’s subject to change.
sa30:14.3: Would a noble disciple see awareness as self, different from self, or that either is present in the other?”
sa30:16.1: “Śroṇa, you should know that whatever forms there are, whether past, future, or present, internal or external, crude or fine, beautiful or ugly, or distant or near, all those forms are not self, not different from self, and neither is present in the other.
sa30:16.2: This is called truly knowing them.
sa30:17.1: “Thus, whatever feelings … conceptions … volitions … instances of awareness there are, whether past, future, or present, internal or external, crude or fine, beautiful or ugly, or distant or near, all those instances of awareness are not self, not different from self, and neither is present in the other.
sa30:17.2: This is called truly knowing them.
sa30:18.1: “In this way, Śroṇa, one becomes disillusioned, becomes free of desire for, and becomes liberated from form, feeling, conception, volition, and awareness.
sa30:18.2: Being liberated, they know and see:
sa30:18.3: ‘My births have been ended, the religious practice has been established, and the task has been accomplished.’
sa30:18.4: They themselves know they won’t be subject to a later existence.”
sa30:19.1: After Śāriputra taught this sūtra, that prominent man’s son Śroṇa was removed from dust, free of defilement, and his Dharma vision became clear.
sa30:19.2: Śroṇa then saw and got the Dharma, and he became confident in the correct Dharma without relying on someone else.
sa30:19.3: He rose from his seat, adjusted his robes to bare his right shoulder, and crouched with his palms together.
sa30:19.6: From this day on, I take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, and take refuge in the Saṅgha as a layman.
sa30:19.7: From today until the end of my life, I will be pure in my devotion to these three jewels.”
sa30:20.1: When the prominent man Śroṇa heard what Śāriputra had taught, he rejoiced and celebrated.
